jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Bhutan governs AI through soft law led by the Government Technology Agency (GovTech): a National AI Strategy (2025), Ethical and Responsible AI Guidelines (2026) with a four-tier risk classification, a 2024 guideline on generative AI use in the civil service issued with the Royal Civil Service Commission, the 2024 Intelligent Bhutan digital strategy and a 2024 AI readiness assessment. The 2025 National Data Governance Framework requires that AI systems' use of data meet legal and safety standards. Bhutan has no AI-specific law and no data protection authority; data privacy rests on the Information, Communications and Media Act 2018.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Not yet verified from the official text: possible AI bills and any central bank AI guidance.

instruments.english_title: Bhutan National AI Strategy (NAIS) 2025: AI for GNH
instruments.issuing_authority: Government Technology Agency (GovTech), Royal Government of Bhutan
instruments.current_status: Published by GovTech as 'National AI Strategy 2025' (PDF uploaded October 2025; listed under Strategies on GovTech's Publications page). The document carries no adoption date or approval statement. Not yet verified from the official text: formal approval by the GovTech Commission.
instruments.summary: Bhutan's first national AI strategy, framed around Gross National Happiness, aiming to move the country from the 'active' to the 'systemic' stage of Gartner's AI maturity model by the end of the 13th Five Year Plan. It sets AI actions in eight key focus areas (agriculture and livestock, tourism, green energy, education, health, public service delivery, natural resources and biodiversity, culture and language) and seven enablers, including a governance-and-regulations enabler that calls for a National Data Governance Framework, national ethical-AI guidelines, a national AI governing body and a review of legislation for AI. It includes monitoring and evaluation and a risk-mitigation section, with action plans reviewed annually and a full review after five years.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; the basis for the 2026 Ethical and Responsible AI Guidelines and a planned national AI governing body.

instruments.issuing_authority: Government Technology Agency (GovTech), Royal Government of Bhutan
instruments.current_status: Dated May 2024 on its cover. Listed as 'GovTech Digital Strategy' under Strategies on GovTech's Publications page. In September 2026 GovTech issued a request for proposals for digital strategy development (see leads), which may lead to a successor.
instruments.summary: GovTech's national digital strategy 'Intelligent Bhutan' structured around digital governance, digital economy and digital society, with enablers on infrastructure, technology adoption, skills, cybersecurity, legislation and R&D in emerging technologies. Its AI content includes using AI/ML to automate routine government tasks (e.g. AI in RCSC and MoICE job portals, document data extraction), AI-driven citizen-service chatbots, AI and AR/VR in education, and attracting investment in AI compute centres; it also commits to reviewing the ICM Act and telecom policy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Digital strategy with AI actions; the National AI Strategy 2025 states it complements the goals of the National Digital Strategy 2024.

instruments.official_title: Guideline for Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage in the Civil Service 2024
instruments.english_title: Guideline for Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage in the Civil Service 2024
instruments.issuing_authority: Royal Civil Service Commission and Government Technology Agency (GovTech)
instruments.current_status: Document dated 2024. Posted on the GovTech website on 19 March 2025 and also hosted on the RCSC website (rcsc.gov.bt uploads, August 2025); the RCSC's September 2025 'Embrace AI' notice directs all civil servants to it. Not yet verified from the official text: the exact issue date.
instruments.summary: Interim guideline, signed by the RCSC Chairperson and the GovTech Secretary, on the ethical and effective use of generative AI by Bhutan's civil servants, prepared with reference to Canadian, UK, Swiss, US, UAE and EU approaches because Bhutan had no AI-specific policy or regulation. It sets risk tiers for AI use, best practices on prompts and data, requires civil servants to fact-check outputs, not to input personal or sensitive data except where unavoidable, to turn off training on user data, and keeps them responsible for AI-assisted content. It links use to the ICM Act 2018, the Civil Liability Act 2023, the Data Management Guide 2023, copyright law and the civil service code of conduct.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First government AI-use rules for the civil service; referenced by the 2026 Ethical and Responsible AI Guidelines.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): GovTech post page (published 2025-03-19) and full PDF read (pdftotext); RCSC copy and RCSC 'Embrace AI' notice read

instruments.official_title: Ethical and Responsible AI Guidelines 2026 Bhutan (Version 1)
instruments.english_title: Ethical and Responsible AI Guidelines (ERAIG) 2026, Bhutan, Version 1
instruments.issuing_authority: Government Technology Agency (GovTech), Data Science & AI Division
instruments.current_status: Version 1, copyright 2026 GovTech; PDF uploaded July 2026 and listed under SOPs/Guidelines on GovTech's Publications page. Expressed in 'encouraged'/'should' terms; no legal force stated.
instruments.summary: National guidelines for all AI actors in Bhutan (public institutions, companies, academia and individuals), grouped as developers, deployers and users, built on six principles: fairness, transparency, responsibility, privacy, safety and reliability. They introduce a four-tier risk-based classification (unacceptable risk systems 'strictly prohibited from development', high, limited and minimal risk) and lifecycle steps for developers (impact assessment, data preparation, testing and documentation), deployers (pre-deployment assessment, pilots, monitoring, decommissioning) and users (consent, oversight, redress). They recommend a feasibility study for an independent National AI Advisory Body and name the GovTech Commission as custodian of ethical and responsible AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Delivers the NAIS action to formulate national guidelines for ethical and responsible AI; Bhutan's main horizontal AI governance document.

instruments.issuing_authority: Royal Government of Bhutan (GovTech Agency) with the United Nations Development Programme
instruments.current_status: Published as 'Bhutan AI Readiness Assessment (AIRA) Report 2024' on GovTech's Publications page (an infographic summary was uploaded March 2025).
instruments.summary: Government assessment of Bhutan's AI readiness using UNDP's AIRA tool across three pillars (government as enabler, government as user, ethical AI) and five readiness phases. It rates the government-as-user pillar 'differentiating' and ethical AI 'opportunistic', finding gaps in AI skills, funding, compute, data governance, oversight and explainability, and recommends a national AI strategy and governance, data governance and interoperability, capacity building and public awareness of AI ethics.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Readiness assessment that the National AI Strategy 2025 explicitly builds on.

instruments.official_title: National Data Governance Framework of Bhutan 2025
instruments.english_title: National Data Governance Framework of Bhutan 2025 (NDGF 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Statistics Bureau, Royal Government of Bhutan
instruments.current_status: Approved and in effect from 11 July 2025 (section 1.1 and foreword). The approving body is not named in the document text read.
instruments.summary: National framework, applicable to all data producers, custodians and users, setting rules on data classification, sharing, quality and interoperability, with a National Data Governance Committee. Pending a national data privacy and protection regulation (which NSB is to lead with GovTech), it sets minimum requirements including a personal-data inventory, encryption, 72-hour breach notification to the sectoral regulator and a duty to 'ensure AI systems align with legal and user safety standards in their data usage'; it also requires protection of data sources including AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Delivers the NAIS action for a National Data Governance Framework and contains explicit AI data-use obligations.

instruments.english_title: Information, Communications and Media Act of Bhutan 2018
instruments.current_status: In force since 8 January 2018 (section 2); the English version is part of the same official bilingual Dzongkha/English text. The Digital Strategy 2024 says the Act will be reviewed and amended.
instruments.summary: Bhutan's consolidated ICT and media law, establishing the Bhutan InfoComm and Media Authority and regulating telecoms, broadcasting, e-government, e-commerce, e-signatures, cyber security and online content. Chapter 17 requires ICT and media service providers to protect users' personal and sensitive personal information and publish privacy policies, and Chapter 21 requires express written consent to collect or process personal information, bars disclosure to third parties without consent or legal basis and requires deletion of obsolete data. It has no AI-specific provisions but its data-protection rules govern AI training and use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main data-protection law; cited by the civil-service GenAI guideline and slated for review under the Digital Strategy.

organizations.name: Government Technology Agency
organizations.ai_governance_role: GovTech Agency of the Royal Government of Bhutan, overseen by the GovTech Commission; leads national digital and AI policy: Digital Strategy (2024), National AI Strategy 2025, Ethical and Responsible AI Guidelines 2026 (Data Science & AI Division), co-author of the civil-service generative AI guideline.

organizations.name: Royal Civil Service Commission
organizations.ai_governance_role: Constitutional body for the civil service; co-issued with GovTech the Guideline for Generative AI Usage in the Civil Service 2024 and the 2025 civil-service AI skills assessment.

organizations.name: National Statistics Bureau
organizations.ai_governance_role: Issuer and custodian of the National Data Governance Framework 2025 (in effect 11 July 2025), which sets data-protection minimums incl. AI data use and is mandated to lead a data privacy and protection regulation.

organizations.name: Parliament of Bhutan
organizations.ai_governance_role: National Assembly and National Council; enacted the Information, Communications and Media Act of Bhutan 2018 (privacy and data protection chapters).
